classification: useful benchmark (framework) / outdated research (last code commit 2021-12-01, README edit 2022-02-22, PyPI 1.34 released 2021-12-01)
benchmarkable: yes (MIT)
notes: WHICH CODECS: Base, Church, Goldman, Grass, Blawat, DNA Fountain, Yin-Yang (7). ECC: Hamming, Reed-Solomon (2). METRICS: information density bits/nt, encode/decode runtime, 'error rate' & recover/success rate after random mutation, GC distribution histogram (0-100%), max homopolymer, share of seqs with GC in 40-60%, max GC bias; OptimalChoicePipeline aggregates these. LICENCE: MIT (c) 2019 BGI-Research. PLUG-IN FEASIBILITY: yes - a VNX codec can be wrapped as subclass of AbstractCodingAlgorithm implementing encode(bit_segments)->list[list[str]] and decode(dna_sequences)->bit_segments (segment-of-bits API, 120-bit default segments, nt as char lists, indexing handled by the pipeline). Limits: it benchmarks only inner mapping + trivial ECC, has no IDS-aware read-level decoding, no clustering, no coverage/dropout model, no real sequencing data - so it cannot evaluate VNX's indel handling. LOCAL TEST (mine, 2026-10-05, Python 3.12.3, numpy 2.5.3, reedsolo 1.7.0): Base/Goldman/Blawat/Church round-trip OK with index=False; YinYangCode raises TypeError ('float' object cannot be interpreted as an integer) in flowed.py addition(): random.randint(total_count+3, math.pow(2,index_length)-1) - float arg rejected by Python >=3.12; Grass needs segment_length divisible by 16; the 'Church' scheme with index=True round-tripped. So the package is bit-rotted on modern Python (needs ~3.7-3.11 or a patch). Last upstream commit 2022-02-22 (README).

purpose: Transcoding (bits->nt) with biochemical constraints; two bit-streams 'yin' and 'yang' combined by a rule table into one nt per two bits; 1536 rule combinations selectable per data type. Inner code only: no indel correction in the repo.

encoding.mapping: Two bits per nt: one binary segment (yang) fixes a base-class by a reference rule [0,1,0,1], the other (yin) selects within class by a 4x4 rule matrix; rule set searched per file ('search_count'); decoding needs the saved model (pickled rule + virtual nucleotide A)
encoding.constrained: yes - candidate segment pairs tested by yyc/utils/validity.py
encoding.motifs: secondary-structure free-energy check via external tool (min_free_energy parameter, subprocess call in validity.py); paper: >= -30 kcal/mol criterion
encoding.addressing: index_operator.py: binary index in front of payload

ecc.rs: not in this repo; the paper used Reed-Solomon (16-bit in vitro, 24-bit in vivo) as outer code per paper summary (my reading via summarizer of PMC text)
ecc.other: ~25-30% logical redundancy reported in paper for wet runs; voting across yeast colonies for in-vivo

error_model.dropout: none in repo (examples/Poisson Generation/poisson.py in ntpz870817/DNA-storage-YYC samples coverage)

benchmarkable: yes (MIT)
notes: Paper-reported (via fetched PMC text, treat numbers as summarised, not re-verified against PDF): up to ~1.95 bits/nt coding potential, 1.75-1.78 bits/nt observed across file types; 10,103 oligos x 200 nt in vitro, 99.9% recovery above 1e4 copies, 87.53% at <=1e2 copies; in vivo ~54 kbp fragment in yeast, 432.2 EB/g physical density, 38.9-95.0% per-colony recovery after ~1000 generations. Physical level: 3 (in vitro synthesis + sequencing; in vivo yeast propagation reported - not a long-term dry archival). Last commit 2025-10-23 'Fix regex pattern in validity' (f1dedbe9b7). Older mirror ntpz870817/DNA-storage-YYC (27 stars, MIT, last code change 2021-06-02). Caveat on novelty: YYC is a constrained mapper; indel robustness comes only from outer RS + physical redundancy, which is why SPIDER-WEB followed.
